messages:
anya: quick update — ran throughput vs latency sweep for streaming (SSE), websocket, and non-streaming http on a100 and h100 in us-west1 + eu-west1.

mike: nice, did you vary concurrency and batch sizes?

anya: yup. concurrency 1..64, batching off/on (max_batch 1, 8, 32). streaming tests used SSE and WS with continuous token streaming. non-streaming = request per-complete (sync).

jordan: what model and sequence lengths?

anya: base-open Llama2-13B-ft, fp16 and int8 quant variants. seq=256 and 1024. perf results are in the CSV I dropped to the gist: https://gist.github.com/rw/infer-bench-1715

sam: any cross-region surprises?

anya: yes — eu-west1 shows ~10-15% higher p99 on streaming at high concurrency on a100. h100 had smaller gap. plausible network headroom + kernel scheduling.

lisa: what about kernel selection? cutlass vs triton?

anya: ran with runtime kernel selector: cutlass for fp16 conv matmuls, triton for some fused attention kernels. I forced triton-only run for comparison.

mike: results?

anya: short summary:
- non-streaming (sync) gives higher throughput at low latency for batched requests (p50 ~ 12ms token on a100 fp16 at batch 32) but p99 spikes with queueing when concurrency uneven.
- streaming (SSE/WS) gives more consistent p99 at low concurrency because tokens are returned incrementally, but overall throughput (tokens/sec) is ~5-18% lower when KV cache can't be reused across many small requests.
- WebSocket vs SSE: nearly identical latency p50/p95 on same infra, WS slightly better under intermittent packet loss.

jordan: does quant help throughput/latency tradeoff?

anya: int8 increases tokens/sec by ~30% on h100 in non-streamed batched runs, p50 token latency improves ~10%. But int8 also had a measurable quality regression on a small eval set (BLEU-ish metric dropped ~1.8 points).

sam: any kernel-level bottlenecks?

anya: attention kernel was the biggest hotspot on seq=1024. triton fused-attention gave better memory locality -> better throughput for long seq. cutlass better for short seq batched matmuls. Runtime choosing per-shape is important.

ops-bot: perf note: noticed OOMs in eu-west1 a100 at batch 32/seq1024 int8 run — suspected driver memory fragmentation.

lisa: did you try prefix/KV cache reuse for streaming endpoints?

anya: yes — enabling prefix KV cache across a session recovers ~12% throughput for streaming under multi-turn, also reduces p99 significantly. But cache hits depend on request routing staying warm to the same GPU.

mike: charts? can you paste the key table here?

anya: pasted abbreviated CSV:
```
mode,gpu,region,quant,seq,concurrency,max_batch,tokens_per_sec,p50_token_ms,p95_token_ms
sync,a100,us-west1,fp16,256,16,32,12000,12,48
stream-sse,a100,us-west1,fp16,256,16,1,10000,14,36
sync,h100,eu-west1,int8,256,16,32,15600,9,30
stream-ws,h100,eu-west1,int8,256,16,1,13000,11,28
sync,a100,us-west1,fp16,1024,8,8,8000,28,120
stream-sse,a100,us-west1,fp16,1024,8,1,6800,30,95
```

jordan: useful. do we have p99 for the high-concurrency edge?

anya: p99s blow up for sync when concurrency >=32 and batch sizing mismatched — observed p99 > 1.2s token. streaming p99 stays sub-400ms in same config.

sam: operational takeaways?

anya:
- prefer non-streamed batched endpoints for throughput-sensitive workloads with predictable request shapes (batching + int8 on h100 gives best tokens/sec).
- prefer streaming endpoints for low-tail-latency interactive apps where you want token-level responsiveness — enable KV cache and session sticky routing to improve throughput.
- enable kernel selector per-shape (triton for long seq, cutlass for short seq).
- run quant evals — int8 gains are real but watch eval/regression thresholds.

lisa: can we add automated perf tests to CI that exercise streaming vs sync patterns across regions?

mike: yes — propose a small nightly that runs 2 workloads (interactive multi-turn streaming, batched bulk sync) on a100/h100 in us-west1+eu-west1 and uploads charts to the perf dashboard.

anya: I'll draft the test + include a gating metric: p99_token < 400ms for streaming at conc=8, tokens/sec delta > +25% for int8 on h100 for sync.

deploy-bot: created perf job: perf/nightly/stream-vs-batched/171525 — queued to runners in us-west1/eu-west1.

mike: awesome. thank you. small next step: can you add a short note on quality regressions for int8 and link the eval prompts?

anya: will do — uploading eval set and diffs to the gist and slack when done. :rocket:
